h: An escape that didn't fit, and a princess remembered
p: Charles I didn't sit quietly as a prisoner here. In 1648 he tried to escape through a window of his rooms, but got stuck between the bars and had to give up. It's a story kids love, and it makes a great talking point as you look at the castle walls.

There's a sadder side to the story too. After the king's execution, two of his children were sent to Carisbrooke, and his daughter Princess Elizabeth died here in 1650, aged just fourteen. Her memorial is in St Thomas's Church in Newport, commissioned by Queen Victoria, and it's a quiet, moving stop if you're in town.
The castle chapel, dedicated to St Nicholas, was rebuilt in the early twentieth century as a memorial to Charles I. It's worth a quiet peek inside.
Princess Beatrice, who made the castle her summer home, was also Governor of the Isle of Wight, so she wasn't just a visitor. She was very much part of island life.
Allow two to three hours for a proper look round, longer if you're bringing a picnic. The walk up from Carisbrooke village to the castle is steep but short.

To round out a royal day, Osborne, Queen Victoria's seaside holiday home near East Cowes, is a short drive away. Newport Roman Villa is a quieter, interesting stop for history buffs, and families might want to add Robin Hill country park or Dinosaur Isle in Sandown for a completely different afternoon.
